Essentially, we need the piece P (as sequence of steps) and a rotated copy P' (rotated by 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°) such that connecting end of P to start of P' and end of P' to start of P forms a simple closed curve. Actually "joining their ends": the two copies joined at both ends to form closed shape. So the closed loop = P followed by transformed P (reversed?). Hmm.

Think: closed shape formed by two copies of the wire joined at endpoints. So the boundary of closed shape consists of wire 1 from endpoint a to b, and wire 2 from b to a (wire 2 is a rotated copy). So the closed curve = P + R(P) where R(P) is the rotated copy traversed from one end to other, connected at ends.

Condition: the concatenation is a simple closed polygon (no self-crossings, no extra contacts).

Equivalently: take P as path from A to B. Take rotated copy P' from A' to B'. Join: B to A' and B' to A? But "joining their ends" probably means the endpoints coincide: i.e., B = A' and B' = A, so the closed curve is P then P'. But then the joint at endpoints: the closed curve is just P followed by P' with shared endpoints. No extra segments.

So we need rotation ρ such that path P (points p0..pn) and path Q = ρ(P) (points q0..qn) with q0 = pn and qn = p0, and the combined closed curve is simple (no self-intersections, no touching elsewhere).

Note Q = ρ(P) means Q's shape is rotated P; its endpoint correspondence: q0 corresponds to p0 or pn? Since identical copy, the copy has its own start/end; when placed, q0 = ρ(p0)+t, qn = ρ(pn)+t. We require {q0, qn} = {p0, pn} with q0 = pn and qn = p0 (so loop closes). Actually could also join p0 to q0 and pn to qn? "joining their ends" ambiguous but likely endpoints matched to form loop: either (p0~q0 and pn~qn) or (p0~qn and pn~q0). Both give loop.
